card.title: Work, torque, angular momentum — vectors in physics dress

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Class 12 vectors pay physics wages: work W = F·d (dot — parallel pays, perpendicular earns nothing), torque τ = r×F (cross — lever arm times force, direction by right-hand rule), angular momentum L = r×p (conserved without external torque). Types (unit, null, like/unlike, collinear, coplanar, free/localised) plus addition laws (triangle, parallelogram, polygon) and scalar multiplication complete the algebra; dot/cross/triple products compute it all.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: W = F·d = |F||d|cosθ (zero at 90°)  ·  τ = r×F, |τ| = rF·sinθ  ·  L = r×p, dL/dt = τ (conserved if τ = 0)  ·  a·b = Σaᵢbᵢ · |a×b| = area of parallelogram  ·  [abc] = determinant = box volume (0 ⟺ coplanar)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Work needs the displacement ALONG the force (components only). Torque needs the perpendicular lever arm (r·sinθ). Angular-momentum conservation needs zero net EXTERNAL torque (internal torques cancel pairwise). Triple-product tests need exactly three 3D vectors.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Satellite in circular orbit: gravity ⊥ velocity → zero work, constant speed (cross-product geometry visible). Door pushing: force at 90° to the panel maximises torque; pushing at the hinge (r → 0) does nothing. Ice-skater spin-up: arms in → I falls → ω rises (L conserved).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Work by F = (3, −1, 2) over d = (2, 1, −1): W = 3·2 + (−1)·1 + 2·(−1) = 6 − 1 − 2 = 3 J. Torque about origin for r = (0, 2, 0), F = (5, 0, 0): τ = r×F = determinant → (0, 0, −10) N·m — clockwise viewed from +z, magnitude 10.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Dot products discard direction (many vectors, one projection). Cross products live in 3D only. Conservation laws need isolated systems — friction/gravity torques quietly drain textbook demos. Component formulas assume orthonormal bases.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Torque from rotation dynamics: tangential F_t = ma_t with a_t = rα → τ = rF_t = mr²α = Iα — Newton's second law in angular dress. Angular momentum: L = r×p differentiates to v×p (= 0, parallel) + r×F = τ — conservation when torque vanishes. Work–energy: integrating F·dr along paths.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Physics-word problems: 'work' → dot; 'moment/turning' → cross magnitude with lever arm; 'spinning/conserved' → L = r×p, set before = after. Perpendicular pairs zero the dot; parallel pairs zero the cross.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB-style: work/torque/L numericals from given vectors; coplanarity verdict via triple product; area of parallelogram/triangle from cross magnitude; projection and angle computations.
